THIS CRL.P FILED U/S.438 CR.P.C PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN THE EVENT OF HIS ARREST IN CR.NO.60/2022 OF LAXMIPURAM P.S., MYSURU CITY FOR THE OFFENCES P/U/S.420, 468, 471 R/W SEC.34 OF IPC PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE 8th ADDITIONAL CIVIL JUDGE (Jr.Dn.)
AND JMFC COURT, JLB COURT, MYSURU CITY.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.60/2022 of Laxmipuram Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468 and 471 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Sri Rajakumar K.R.
2. Heard Sri.Srinivas N., learned Counsel for the petitioner and Sri.H.S.Shankar, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials placed on record.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are arrayed as accused Nos.1 and 2.
They are innocent and law abiding citizens.
They have not committed any offence as alleged.
They have been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
The main grievance of the first informant is only against the RTO officials.
However, these petitioners are named as accused Nos.1 and 2.

The police have issued notice under Section 41 of Cr.P.C.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the petitioners are in possession of all the relevant documents.
Therefore, they are not required for custodial interrogation.
The petitioners are running the reputed Driving School in Mysuru since several years.
They are the permanent residents of the addresses mentioned in the cause title to the petition and are ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition in the interest of justice.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioners for having committed the offences.

Specifically, the names of these petitioners are mentioned by the informant, who has given details of some of the fake driving licences that were obtained in collusion with the petitioners, RTO officials and other persons who are acting as brokers, under the guise of running the driving school.
Therefore, the petitioners are absconding since the date of the registration of the case.
Looking to the nature and seriousness of the offences, the petitioners are required for custodial interrogation.

If the petitioners are granted anticipatory bail, they may never turn up before the Investigating Officer and they may abscond or may commit similar offences, threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.

Therefore,
the petitioners are not entitled for grant of pre- arrest bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text:
In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 7.
The allegations made by the informant against these petitioners are of serious nature.

It is alleged that the petitioners under the guise of running the driving school, are acting as middlemen, are colluding with the RTO officials in Mysuru and they are managed to get the fake driving licence by furnishing false information.
It is also stated that the names and address mentioned in the driving licences referred to in the first information are all fake.
Even photos are not affixed and such persons obtained driving licence without LLR.
Some of these driving licences issued during period of 2018.
It is also alleged that the accused have forged the signatures including the digital signatures of RTO officials.
The informant also stated that these petitioners have submitted some of the documents relating to the driving school mentioned in the first information.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be concluded that there are no allegations against these petitioners for having committed the offences.
The allegations made against the petitioners are of serious nature and it will have a serious consequences.
Under such circumstances, the petitioners are required for custodial interrogation by the Investigation Officer, who has to conduct a detailed investigation.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioners are not entitled for pre-arrest bail.

8. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
